newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico cracks down on drug trafficking.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico cracks down on drug trafficking.

text.p: The U.S. Border Patrol and New Mexico state police on Saturday announced stepped-up patrols along the Mexico-New Mexico border aimed at reducing illegal immigration and narcotics-trafficking in the region.

New Mexico has experienced a 50 percent increase in drug-trafficking and a 60 percent increase in illegal immigration in the past few years since Texas, Arizona and California started cracking down along their borders with Mexico, officials said.
"We need to let everyone know that this region of the country is not a thoroughfare," U.S. Border Patrol Assistant Chief Robert Saenz said.

Under the new programme, code-named "Operation High Point," agents will be positioned every quarter-mile (.4 km) along a critical 10-mile (16 km) stretch of New Mexico's southern border with Mexico. Agents also will increase patrols along other sections of the border on foot, in cars and on horseback.
During a trial run over the past two weeks, drug seizures increased 104 percent and the capture of illegal immigrants went up 59 percent, officials said.

Deming Police Chief Mike Carillo said they also noticed a decline in violent crime, which has escalated recently as New Mexico became a gateway for drug-traffickers moving marijuana and cocaine across the border from Mexico.
